source.title: CytoSAE: Interpretable Cell Embeddings for Hematology
source.authors: Muhammed Furkan Dasdelen; Hyesu Lim; M. Buck; K. Götze; C. Marr; Steffen Schneider

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies SAE concept discovery in hematology and reports how latent counts vary with expansion factor, but it does not test feature splitting, feature correspondence, or partitioning of inputs.
record.gate_note: The expansion-factor counts and the statement that the highly activated cluster remained relatively stable concern latent counts, not whether larger-dictionary features split or align with smaller-dictionary features. They are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. The paper also reports ablations of other hyperparameters; those do not bear on the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper trains a vision SAE on DinoBloom-B hematology embeddings to find morphological concepts. It cites Towards Monosemanticity only for the L1 objective and ghost-gradient resampling. It never matches features across dictionary sizes or measures splitting, absorption, hierarchy or decomposition. The expansion-factor sweep reports only how many latents pass a mean-activation threshold, which is a hyperparameter ablation for choosing the SAE. 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses', because feature splitting is never discussed.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that CytoSAE learns interpretable morphological concepts that generalize across peripheral blood and bone marrow datasets. They also conclude it supports patch-, image-, patient- and disease-level analysis, with AML subtype classification near state of the art (weighted F1 0.832±0.044). They draw no conclusion about feature splitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a vision SAE on DinoBloom-B hematology residual activations, using reconstruction MSE and an L1 sparsity regularizer, and varies expansion factor. It does not perform matched-feature analysis across sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported number of latents above the -3 threshold changes with expansion factor; the paper also states that the high-activation cluster count remained relatively stable.

fits_no_version.finding: At a log10 mean-activation threshold of -3, latents above threshold rise from 1748±56 (expansion 16) to 3518±145 (expansion 128). The high-activation cluster is described as relatively stable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a hematology vision SAE, larger expansion factors add latents above a mean-activation threshold sublinearly, while the high-activation cluster stays roughly constant in size.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
record.problems: The size-related results are latent counts rather than measurements of cross-size feature correspondence, direction similarity, or input partitioning. The text does not specify what the reported ± values represent.

untested.parts: All of it. There is no cross-size feature matching, direction similarity or input coverage analysis.
All of it. There is no splitting analysis in large models or open SAE releases.
All of it. There are no feature families or hierarchy geometry.
All of it. There is no parent/child latent firing or absorption measure.
All of it. There is no decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents and no count of novel latents.
All of it. Only the L1 coefficient is varied, for concept counts, and no alternative objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs are compared.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only', because splitting is never discussed. The text does not define the ± values; each experiment was run with three seeds. The sweep's other ablations (L1 coefficient, layer, learning rate, ghost gradients) also report only concept counts and bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No feature matching across dictionary sizes, directional similarity, or input-set partitioning is measured.
The paper uses a vision model in hematology, but does not test the claimed splitting pattern in large models or open SAE releases.
No nested feature families or geometric relationships between split features are measured.
No parent-child activation overlap, absorption, or effect of size or sparsity on absorption is tested.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents or analysis of novel latents is reported.
The paper uses an L1 sparsity regularizer but does not test whether the sparsity objective produces splitting or compare objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs.
